With the elections only days away, the Trump administration is resorting to
even more alarming efforts to interfere with the midterm elections.

In recent weeks, the president's Justice Department has ramped up its
targeting of Donald Trump's political enemies, despite [long-standing
precedent](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/justice-department/dojs-shocking-
flurry-pre-election-activity-breaks-long-standing-preced-
rcna605920?cid=sm_npd_nn_tw_ma&taid=6ae2464325edfb00017cefba&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter)
to avoid taking actions that could influence elections. This week saw former
FBI Director James Comey
[charged](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/26/us/politics/james-comey-charges-
doj.html) for the third time in 13 months, while a grand jury
[declined](https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/10/27/grand-
jury-declines-indict-cassidy-hutchinson-over-jan-6-testimony/) to indict
former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson over her Jan. 6 testimony.

Meanwhile, FBI agents are [worried](https://www.ms.now/news/white-house-
actions-spur-worry-among-fbi-agents-about-being-called-to-polling-places-
sources-say) about being ordered to seize voting machines, Trump has
effectively [called](https://alaskabeacon.com/2026/10/28/trump-calls-for-
peltola-to-be-criminally-charged-removed-from-alaskas-u-s-senate-race/) for
the Alaska Senate election to be canceled and the prosecution of Democratic
nominee Mary Peltola, and as _Wired_
[reported](https://www.wired.com/story/ice-is-running-one-of-the-largest-anti-
left-surveillance-operations-in-us-history/), ICE is carrying out one of the
largest anti-left surveillance operations in the history of the United States.

And as all of this is happening, a new [rape
allegation](https://zeteo.com/p/why-is-the-media-ignoring-trump) against the
U.S. president barely made headlines.

From expanding a criminal investigation into California voters to threatening
election officials with criminal prosecution, here's just a taste of what
Trump and his cronies did this week that harmed democracy, undermined the U.S.
Constitution, and hurt societies worldwide:

#### **Saturday, Oct. 24 - White House Might Issue Blanket Pardons to Junior
Staff**

The Washington Sun [reported](https://www.washingtonsun.com/whitehouse/white-
house-weighing-mass-pardons-for-junior-staff) that the White House is looking
into issuing mass pardons for junior staff, a move that has been pushed by
several conservative organizations including the Heritage Foundation.

While one source says it's unlikely Trump would pardon all junior
administration staffers, the president could issue pardons for employees in
specific policy areas, like deportations or war.

#### **Sunday, Oct. 25 - Trump's Racist and Islamophobic Attacks Against Abdul
El-Sayed**

Trump [ramped up](https://apnews.com/article/trump-michigan-elsayed-rogers-
senate-midterms-162330c3d193ecb94538f8dd8083f916) his Islamophobic attacks
against Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic Senate nominee in Michigan, calling him
a "jihadist" and that he should "have to go through a metal detector before
he's allowed to go into the Senate." He also
[said](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/25/us/elections/trump-michigan-el-
sayed-rogers.html) "any Jewish person that supports this guy should be ashamed
of themselves."

Later, El-Sayed clapped back at Trump's racist comments, saying, "I'll go
through a metal detector if you'll sit for a lie detector."

#### **Monday, Oct. 26 - Trump Administration Charges James Comey… Again**

The Trump administration
[charged](https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.dcd.297298/gov.uscourts.dcd.297298.1.0.pdf)
James Comey with two counts under the Espionage Act, marking the third time
the former FBI director has been charged by the president's Justice Department
in just 13 months. The charges accused Comey of mishandling national security
information. Comey was charged via criminal information rather than a grand
jury, as Trump officials sought to get the charges in under the wire, before
the statute of limitations ran out.

In a video, Comey [said](https://jamescomey.substack.com/p/yet-another-case-
now) he was innocent of the charges, and noted the new case against him "would
almost be funny if it weren't such an appalling abuse of the Department of
Justice, one that we cannot become numb to."

The charges were unsealed the same day a federal judge
[ruled](https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/trump-administrations-firing-
prosecutor-maurene-comey-was-unlawful-judge-rules-2026-10-26/) the Trump
administration illegally fired his daughter, prosecutor Maurene Comey.

#### **Tuesday, Oct. 27 - Supreme Court Signs Off on Eliminating Immigration
Rule**

The Supreme Court
[allowed](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/27/us/politics/supreme-court-texas-
immigration.html) the Trump administration to move forward with the
elimination of a Biden-era policy giving immigration judges the ability to
suspend some deportation proceedings, including when someone is seeking
humanitarian protections or other legal status.

The move was part of an unusual settlement agreement, between Trump's Justice
Department and the state of Texas, that opponents have described as "egregious
collusion."

#### **Wednesday, Oct. 28 - FBI Agents Fear Having to Seize Voting Machines**

MS NOW [reported](https://www.ms.now/news/white-house-actions-spur-worry-
among-fbi-agents-about-being-called-to-polling-places-sources-say) that recent
White House actions have raised concerns among some FBI agents who fear that
they may be ordered to seize voting machines or undertake other measures that
could interfere with the results of the midterm elections.

Meanwhile, Reuters [reported](https://www.reuters.com/world/us/trump-expands-
hunt-noncitizen-voters-with-broad-subpoena-campaign-before-2026-10-28/) that
the Trump administration has issued more than 100 subpoenas in an effort to
acquire voting records for tens of thousands of people across at least 13
states as part of its push to find noncitizen voters, which has already been
proven to be [exceedingly rare](https://protectdemocracy.org/work/noncitizen-
voting-lies-explained/).

#### **Thursday, Oct. 29 - Trump Administration Expands California Voter
Investigation**

The _New York Times_ [reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/trump-
doj-california-voter-rolls-midterms.html?smtyp=cur&smid=tw-nytimes) that the
Trump administration is expanding its criminal investigation into California,
issuing grand jury subpoenas to local election officials in relation to the
Justice Department's unsubstantiated claim that thousands of noncitizens are
on the state's voter rolls.

Meanwhile, Trump's Department of Justice
[sent](https://www.votebeat.org/national/2026/10/30/doj-election-officials-
criminal-prosecution-letters-2026-midterms/) letters to election officials in
all 50 states warning that they could face criminal prosecution if they
violate any federal election laws, despite a federal judge warning the Trump
administration this week to stop threatening election workers.

#### **Friday, Oct. 30 - Trump Admin Plans One of the Largest Single
Expulsions of Afghans**

The _Times_ [reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/30/world/asia/afghan-
refugees-deported-flight-pakistan.html?smid=tw-nytimes&smtyp=cur) that dozens
of Afghan immigrants have been detained in Louisiana by the Trump
administration, which plans to deport them to Pakistan, where they are
expected to be removed to Afghanistan.

More than 150 Afghans are expected to be deported, according to the _Times_ ,
which would be one of the largest single expulsions of Afghans. Among those
slated to be deported are several who could face discrimination or persecution
by the Taliban, including relatives of people who assisted the U.S. military
and at least one gay man.
